ch17-open.title: Leaving & review
ch17-open.standfirst: Every meeting has a way out, and most have an afterlife. This chapter covers the difference between hanging up your call, walking out of the room, and the moment a host ends the meeting for everyone — and what a finished meeting lets you do when you open it again to read the record.

ch17-three-exits.heading: Three ways to step out — and they are not the same
ch17-three-exits.lead: Canvas M deliberately gives leaving three distinct verbs, each with its own glyph in the header, so you never confuse a small step back with shutting the whole room down.
ch17-three-exits.body: Leave call (a hang-up handset in the media group) only drops you out of the live audio/video — you stay in the meeting, the canvas is still live, and you can rejoin the call with Join. Leave (an arrow-out-of-box icon, far right) exits the meeting room entirely: your canvas is saved, the room is cleared from the URL so you won't auto-rejoin on reload, and you land back on your project home. Everyone else stays. End meeting (a red power icon) is the host-only kill switch — it finishes the meeting for everyone at once.
ch17-three-exits.pull: Leave call = hang up. Leave = walk out. End meeting = power off the room.

diagram.label: The three exit glyphs
diagram.cap: Left to right: hang-up (Leave call), arrow-out (Leave), red power (End meeting).

note.html: The red End meeting button only appears for the host, organiser, co-host, or a project authority. If you don't see it, you can't end the meeting for everyone — and that's by design. The server enforces the same rule, so the button's absence is not the only guard.

ch17-leave.heading: Leaving the meeting
steps: Find the Leave button at the far-right edge of the header (the arrow-out-of-box icon).
Click it. There's no confirmation prompt — leaving is a safe, reversible action.
Your canvas is saved automatically before the connection closes.
The room is removed from the address bar, so a reload won't pull you back in.
You return to your project home, where the meeting may still be offered as Resume meeting if it's still running.
ch17-leave.outcome: You're out of the room. The meeting carries on for everyone who stayed, and you can re-open it any time it's still live.
ch17-leave.note: If the host removes you from the meeting, you'll see a notice and then be taken out the same way — you don't have to click Leave yourself.
ch17-leave.figcap: The Leave button sits in the header's exit group, away from the live media controls so it's never hit by accident.

ch17-ended.heading: When the host ends the meeting
ch17-ended.lead: Ending is the host's call, and it's final. When the host clicks End meeting, they first confirm the prompt “End the meeting for EVERYONE? All participants switch to read-only review.” — and that's exactly what happens to you.
ch17-ended.body: Within a second or two, your meeting flips into review mode without dropping you. The canvas becomes read-only, a banner appears across the top, and the meeting is marked finished. You don't get kicked out — you can stay and read the record, download the transcript, or step out with Leave whenever you're ready. Behind the scenes the meeting is recorded as finished so that re-opening it later always lands you back in this same read-only review.

note.html: Ending also kicks off an automatic AI recap from the transcript and chat — it runs in the background and never delays the meeting from ending. You'll find that recap surfaced later in the meeting's detail view.

ch17-review-states.heading: What review mode locks — and what it leaves open

tiles.cap: A status banner reads “Reviewing (read-only) · meeting finished — extract only” with an eye icon, pinned to the canvas so you always know the meeting is frozen.
The conversation panel shows “Reviewing a finished meeting — chat is read-only”. You can read every message but can't send new ones.
Uploads are disabled: “The meeting has finished — the library is read-only, uploads are disabled.” Existing files stay viewable.

ch17-review-states.useWhen: You'll see all three together the moment a meeting finishes — whether the host ended it live, or you opened a finished meeting from your portal or project list. Content-creating tools (stickers, the canvas bot, text translation) are hidden, and you can't present or edit the meeting's title.

ch17-log.heading: Reading the transcript & generating a summary
steps: Open the log from the header's Transcript button (the document icon — it shows a count badge when there's a transcript).
The log opens on the Transcript tab: the full conversation, grouped by speaker with avatars, timestamps, and a per-line language tag.
Switch to the Summary tab. If none exists yet, click Generate summary — Gemini reads the full transcript and returns an overview, participants, key topics, decisions, and action items.
Watch for “Generating summary… (~5-15s for long meetings)”; a dot appears on the Summary tab once it's ready.
Click Download .md to save the current tab (transcript or summary) as a Markdown file.
Press <kbd>Esc</kbd> or click outside the modal to close it.
ch17-log.outcome: You've read the record and, if you wanted, pulled a structured recap and a downloadable copy — without changing anything in the finished meeting.

host.html: In a live meeting the footer also offers Clear log (wipes the transcript and summary for the room after a confirm) and Regenerate summary. Both are hidden in review — a finished meeting is extract-only, so you can read and download but never rewrite the record.

ch17-log.figcap: The meeting log modal: Transcript and Summary tabs, with download in the footer.

ch17-log-ref.heading: Every button in the meeting log
rows: Full chronological transcript, grouped by speaker
AI overview, topics, decisions, action items
Asks Gemini for a recap of the transcript
Replaces an existing summary with a fresh one
Saves the active tab as a Markdown file
Wipes transcript + summary for the room (confirm)
ch17-log-ref.note: The transcript only fills up while someone has speech-to-text turned on during the call. An empty log reads “No transcript yet. Join a call + turn on STT to start recording.”

host.html: Clearing a log empties what you see immediately, but the stored transcript blob still exists — rejoining the room re-hydrates it.

ch17-trouble.heading: Leaving & review troubleshooting

rows.cause: You're not the host, organiser, co-host, or project authority
rows.fix: Only those roles can end a meeting for everyone. Use Leave to exit yourself; ask the host to end it.
Expected. You're now in review — read the transcript, download it, or click Leave. Nothing you do can edit it.
Chat is read-only in a finished meeting by design. You can still read every message.
Uploads are off in a finished meeting — the library is read-only. Open existing files to view them.
Click Generate summary on the Summary tab. Hidden in review — read or download instead.

rows.sym: “Couldn't end the meeting — check your network and try again.”
rows.cause: The finish write to the server failed (host action)
rows.fix: Nothing changed; the host can simply retry End meeting.

rows.sym: Re-opened a meeting and it's read-only
rows.cause: The meeting is finished — it always opens for review
rows.fix: Expected. A finished meeting is immutable and extract-only every time you open it.

ch17-trouble.note: Leaving never loses work — your canvas is saved before the room closes. Ending is the only irreversible exit, and only a host can do it.
